method: Reviewed historical additions within 2020–2026. Earlier July–October 2026 research is retained; the 2020-onward backfill is an initial, incomplete collection. Publication dates govern sorting and date filters; event dates and country roles remain separate. No absence implies inactivity.

signals.t: Benin opens AI summer school with 190 selected learners
signals.note: Benin hosted the programme; the other countries are explicitly named as participants' origins. The 190 places are a multinational cohort, not a count for each country or jobs created.

signals.t: Togo announces AI summer school targeting 100 participants
signals.note: Scheduled training in Lome. The stated 100 is a target; this article does not verify attendance, completion or employment.

signals.t: University of Liberia consults on a proposed MSc in AI
signals.note: UNDP describes stakeholder consultations and accreditation work. The degree is proposed, not confirmed as accredited or delivering graduates.

signals.t: Liberia: Liblaw unveils CJ Lewis legal-information AI assistant
signals.note: Local reporting describes a launch and provider claims about access to legal information. Accuracy, usage and effects on legal services have not been independently measured.

signals.t: Guinea reviews plans for a national AI and data strategy
signals.s: Guinea Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research
signals.note: The ministry reports discussions following a Blueprint workshop. This is strategy preparation, not evidence of adoption or completed deployment.

signals.t: Botswana and Namibia discuss responsible AI use in higher education
signals.note: Workshop in Windhoek involved institutions from both countries. Global UNESCO survey percentages are not national adoption estimates. Page updated 24 August 2026.

signals.t: UNDP reports lessons from AI compute deployments in six African countries
signals.note: Publisher summary covers Malawi, Rwanda, Togo, Zambia, Kenya and South Africa. Deployment, activation and operation are distinct stages; no GPU inventory or MW value is inferred from this page.

signals.t: CIPIT publishes AI policy review covering Rwanda, Tanzania, Uganda and Kenya
signals.note: Publisher description establishes report scope. It does not rank countries or demonstrate adoption or economic impact; individual policy claims require reading the underlying documents.

signals.t: Tunisia hosts AI-Forward summit and adoption of AI4ALL declaration
signals.note: Organizer report from Yasmine Hammamet. A declaration and discussions do not establish implementation, investment delivered or national adoption.

signals.t: Algeria reviews AI infrastructure, model and training implementation plans
signals.s: Algeria Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research
signals.note: Arabic ministry report distinguishes planned infrastructure/data actions, existing servers and GPUs, model progress and proposed training. No capacity, budget or employment outcome is inferred. This is the third coordination meeting on 21 September, a follow-up to the August roadmap and September committee-creation signals already retained.

signals.t: Ethiopia reports graduation of first AI institute startup-training cohort
signals.note: ENA reports a graduation ceremony after six months of training. Cohort size and jobs created are not given; broad official impact claims are not treated as measured outcomes.

signals.t: Mozambique discusses AI regulatory sandboxes at forum in Angola
signals.note: Mozambique is the participating regulator and Angola the host. Discussion of sandbox design is not proof that an operational AI sandbox has been launched.

signals.t: Mozambique: FUNDEC presents proposals linking AI and business competitiveness
signals.note: Organizer account of an economic forum and AI study. Suggested applications and a future roadmap are proposals; reported economic indicators are not attributed to AI.

signals.t: Eswatini hosts COMESA review of draft AI and emerging-technology study
signals.note: Eswatini is the meeting host. The statement is dated 16 September and posted 25 September. Regional strategy and regulatory instruments are future work, not enacted national law.

signals.t: Sierra Leone ministry reports soft launch of WAKABOT tourism chatbot
signals.s: Sierra Leone Ministry of Tourism and Cultural Affairs
signals.note: The ministry describes a trip planner and chatbot soft launch; analytics remain a later phase. Publication date is shown in the ministry news listing. No independent user or economic-impact measurement.

signals.t: Seychelles approves AI-in-education framework and describes school pilots
signals.note: Presidency reports framework approval and teacher-coach and student-tutor pilots. These are limited pilots, not nationwide use or independently demonstrated learning gains.

signals.t: Senegal hosts UEMOA forum on AI and financial inclusion
signals.s: Senegal Ministry of Economy, Finance and Planning
signals.note: Dakar is the host. The source discusses responsible AI in banking; it does not quantify deployment or financial-inclusion gains for Senegal or every UEMOA member.

signals.t: Mauritius demonstrates parliamentary AI to Seychelles, Comoros and Madagascar delegates
signals.note: Mauritius is the host; the other countries supplied visiting delegates. Participation does not establish that visiting parliaments deployed AI.

signals.t: Burundi presents AI infrastructure and skills priorities at KOAFEC
signals.note: Secondary reporting on policy priorities and proposed partnerships. Planned training and pilots are not completions; no new funded facility or operating capacity is established.

signals.t: Eritrean institute reports graduates from introductory AI courses
signals.note: Interview with Polytech's founder reports about 50 AI-course graduates during 2026 to date. This is a provider claim, not independently audited, and not a count of jobs created. Exact course and graduation dates are unstated.

signals.t: Malawi reviews preliminary findings of its AI readiness assessment
signals.s: National Commission for Science and Technology, Malawi
signals.note: The commission reports a stakeholder workshop on preliminary readiness findings. This does not establish an adopted AI strategy, deployed systems or measured economic gains.

signals.t: Mauritius launches AI-assisted water-leak reporting in KOREK
signals.s: Mauritius Ministry of ICT and Innovation
signals.note: The ministry says AI helps triage the severity of photo-and-location reports for the water authority. No usage, model accuracy, water savings or independently evaluated impact is published in this announcement.

signals.t: Togo opens paid contributions for a local-language AI pilot
signals.note: Voix du Togo seeks voice and text contributions for Kabye, Ewe and Moba, with UNDP support. Paid contribution tasks are not a count of permanent jobs. Wider language coverage and public-service access are ambitions, not established outcomes.

signals.t: Cameroon and Morocco discuss AI cooperation for public administration
signals.s: Cameroon Ministry of Public Service and Administrative Reform
signals.note: The ministerial account discusses possible AI use for administrative tasks and proposed bilateral cooperation. It does not demonstrate an AI deployment or signed implementation contract. The existing AIGLES payroll system is not reclassified as AI.

signals.t: Mozambique agrees cooperation on a digital-health laboratory and AI sandbox
signals.note: INTIC and INS report a five-year agreement for laboratory, digital-health and AI-sandbox cooperation. Facilities and sandbox implementation are prospective; the agreement is not proof of an operating AI system. This is distinct from the September regional sandbox discussion.

signals.t: Rwanda statistics team reports AI-assisted survey coding
signals.note: The programme partner describes a model supporting survey analysts in Kinyarwanda, English and French. Its 96% auto-coding result concerns one reported test, not national AI accuracy. Reported workflow savings do not establish layoffs; an enumerator app remains a future step.

signals.t: Researchers present a shiKomori educational AI assistant
signals.note: The Mwando preprint describes support for four shiKomori varieties and an evaluation on 500 queries. This is author-reported research, not independently verified deployment, user adoption or economic impact. The country tag identifies the language context, not proof of operation throughout Comoros.

signals.t: Makerere invites applications for AI doctoral fellowships
signals.note: The call covers health, language processing, agriculture and environment, with an application deadline of 24 August 2026. It does not report successful applicants, completed training or jobs created. The historical call is no longer presented as an open opportunity.

signals.t: AI Institute of South Africa launched
signals.note: The speech’s proposed future hubs and school rollout are not recorded here as completed.

signals.t: AI and big-data strategy approved
signals.note: The published multi-year budget is a planned amount, not evidence of disbursement or results.

signals.t: National AI strategy presented
signals.note: The minister described implementation as forthcoming. Presentation is not deployment.

signals.t: AI readiness assessment handed over
signals.note: The June 5 publication does not establish the exact day of the handover; recommendations are not implementation.

signals.t: AI readiness assessment launched
signals.note: The article was published on August 14; it does not independently specify the launch day. An assessment is not a readiness score adopted by this site.

signals.t: Botswana and Malawi consult on draft AI readiness assessments
signals.note: Draft-report consultation does not establish final publication or adoption of a national AI strategy. The reviewed source reports consultations, not deployment or a completed strategy. One shared report, not separate national deployments. Country roles differ: see the original source.

signals.t: UNESCO reports AI education framework work in four African pilot countries
signals.note: Participation by Benin does not mean the workshop took place in Benin. A framework under development is not classroom-wide AI adoption. Country participation is documented; a completed national framework or nationwide rollout is not established. This records programme participation only; it does not date or establish a separate national AI policy. One shared report, not separate national deployments. Country roles differ: see the original source.

signals.t: UNESCO readiness assessment process launched
signals.note: The November 28 article dates the report; the event day is not separately supplied. This is initiation, not completion.

signals.t: Nigeria inaugurates AI and robotics centre in Abuja
signals.note: Contemporaneous inauguration report, corroborated by NCAIR’s institutional history. Facility opening does not establish utilisation or economic impact.

signals.t: Togo’s rural cash-transfer expansion uses machine learning
signals.note: CEGA’s dated account of the November ML-assisted expansion. The original April 2020 Novissi launch preceded this phase. Programme-wide beneficiaries must not all be attributed to machine learning.

signals.t: World Bank reports on ML targeting in Togo’s Novissi programme
signals.note: The report describes the November 2020–March 2021 targeting phase. It is follow-up evidence for the same programme, not a new launch or a new total to add to other Novissi cohorts.

signals.t: InstaDeep and BioNTech announce joint AI drug-discovery lab
signals.note: Tunisia tag denotes InstaDeep’s Tunisian origins and Tunis presence, not that this international transaction or laboratory is based wholly in Tunisia. No investment amount is assigned to domestic Tunisian AI spending. The announced lab locations are London and Mainz. Intended research benefits are not clinical outcomes.

signals.t: InstaDeep closes Series B funding round
signals.note: Tunisia tag denotes InstaDeep’s Tunisian origins and Tunis presence, not that this international transaction or laboratory is based wholly in Tunisia. No investment amount is assigned to domestic Tunisian AI spending.

signals.t: BioNTech announces agreement to acquire InstaDeep
signals.note: Tunisia tag denotes InstaDeep’s Tunisian origins and Tunis presence, not that this international transaction or laboratory is based wholly in Tunisia. No investment amount is assigned to domestic Tunisian AI spending. This is the agreement announcement; completion is a separate July 2023 follow-up.

signals.t: BioNTech completes acquisition of InstaDeep
signals.note: Tunisia tag denotes InstaDeep’s Tunisian origins and Tunis presence, not that this international transaction or laboratory is based wholly in Tunisia. No investment amount is assigned to domestic Tunisian AI spending. The acquired company remains a UK-based global subsidiary. Do not count announcement and completion as two acquisitions.

signals.t: Makerere announces DeepMind-backed AI scholarships
signals.note: The university announced four scholarships for the 2021/22 academic year. This report establishes the planned programme, not subsequent enrolment, completion or employment. Uganda is the host; wider eligibility is not a deployment in every eligible country.

signals.t: Congo and ECA schedule AI research centre inauguration
signals.note: Published before the scheduled opening. The prospective opening date is not proof of completion. The institution is in the Republic of the Congo, not the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The source’s Africa-first claim is not adopted as a verified ranking.

signals.t: Congo’s AI research centre inaugurated at Kintélé
signals.note: The dated report confirms the opening; ECA’s project page separately gives 24 February 2022: https://www.uneca.org/fr/node/7975 . This follows the announcement of the same centre, not a second facility. Research, training and job-creation ambitions are not measured economic results.

signals.t: Windhoek forum discusses inclusive AI governance
signals.note: UNESCO’s follow-up describes the Southern Africa forum held on 7–9 September. Namibia hosted a regional discussion; this is not proof of AI deployment or policy adoption across all SADC countries. Publication was 29 September, not the later webpage update.

signals.t: Senegal university documents AI development research initiative
signals.note: The webpage is dated 26 April 2023 but explicitly describes a 15 December 2021 ceremony in Dakar. It documents research to inform responsible AI strategies. It does not establish strategy adoption or deployment in each West African country mentioned in the research scope.

signals.t: Mozambique hosts coding camp with AI and robotics training
signals.note: ECA reports a week-long camp in Chimoio and participants from Mozambique and Angola. AI was one component of broader ICT training. The cohort is shared, not a separate total per country; the initiative-wide alumni total is not an AI-trainee or employment count.

signals.t: Study examines educators’ views on AI in Lesotho, Rwanda and Nigeria
signals.s: Theodorio and colleagues / Education and Information Technologies
signals.note: The paper uses an online semi-structured questionnaire with a sampled group of educators. Its perspectives and barriers are not representative national AI adoption rates, verified institutional deployments or measured learning gains. The event date is publication, not the unspecified fieldwork date.

signals.t: UNDP and University of Eswatini sign AI research agreement
signals.note: A two-year agreement covers AI/ML research, student training and testing tools for development programming. The report confirms signing but does not separately date the ceremony. Planned activities and benefits are not completed research outcomes.

signals.t: Eswatini AI Indaba discusses national strategy plans
signals.note: The UN reports an AI Indaba in Ezulwini and plans to develop AI and Fourth Industrial Revolution strategies in fiscal 2024/25. It does not establish their adoption, financing or delivery. The article publication date is not substituted for an unstated event day.

signals.t: Guinean developers demonstrate local-language AI prototype
signals.note: Original reporting and developer interviews describe Nma Xui at an early prototype stage. Language-data scarcity and speech quality remain challenges. This is not a nationwide service, independent accuracy evaluation or a national adoption measure.

signals.t: Mauritius Cabinet agrees to volunteer for Commonwealth AI initiative
signals.note: Item 8 on page 4 records agreement to volunteer as a Commonwealth Champion Country for an initiative then being developed. It is a Cabinet decision, not a national rollout, a new AI strategy or independently confirmed completion of the Commonwealth role.

signals.t: Djibouti ports authority presents predictive logistics and road-monitoring AI
signals.s: Djibouti Ports and Free Zones Authority
signals.note: The authority describes DPCS Foresight and DPCR Vision AI at the national forum, and dates the latter’s launch to 2024. The article remains 2026 news; its claims about efficiency gains are provider-reported, without an independent impact evaluation. The two applications are not counted as two new October launches.

signals.t: UNESCO and Smart Africa train judicial participants from 13 countries
signals.note: One online course for participants from 13 named countries, not 13 national programmes or country-wide judicial adoption. Article-level survey percentages are not country-specific estimates. Training participation does not establish official AI rules, continuing use or economic results.

review_rounds.scope: Initial dated candidates; not a systematic 54-country census
Selected undercovered countries and 2021–2024 leads, plus dated 2026 follow-through. Not a systematic census.
